Liam O'Connor: hey team — first day. Trying to run the dotfiles bootstrap under Git Bash/MSYS2 on Windows and running into permission/symlink errors. bootstrap.sh fails with 'Operation not permitted' when creating symlinks.

I tried: 
```
# Git Bash
git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/dotfiles.git ~/dotfiles
cd ~/dotfiles
./bootstrap.sh
```

Priya Nair (DevEx): welcome Liam! :wave: Two quick paths: use WSL2 (preferred) or make the bootstrap copy files instead of symlinking. For MSYS/Git Bash you can enable developer mode or run Git Bash as admin to allow symlinks, but often easiest is: `export USE_COPY=1 && ./bootstrap.sh` which makes safe copies.

Priya Nair (DevEx): If you want symlinks in MSYS, install MSYS2 pacman packages that provide correct POSIX behavior: `pacman -Syu coreutils git bash ln` and ensure your HOME is on a native filesystem (not a mounted Windows network share). Also check `git config core.symlinks true`.

Liam O'Connor: export USE_COPY=1 worked — bootstrap finished and config files are in place. Curious if there's a recommended long-term approach — we plan to use asdf for runtime parity.

Priya Nair (DevEx): long-term: WSL2 if you can get it via IT; it aligns with CI and infra. For asdf on Git Bash, prefer cloning asdf into `~/.asdf` (not brew) and source it from `~/.bashrc`:
```
# in ~/.bashrc
. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"
```
Then asdf works the same.

Dotfiles Bot: Canonical docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles (see docs/windows.md and docs/wsl.md).

IT Support Bot: Need admin to enable WSL2? File a ticket: https://internal.redwood.com/helpdesk (choose "Developer laptop admin").

Liam O'Connor: thanks all — copying files is fine for now, will file the WSL ticket. :thumbsup:
